fields.features_heading: What Emergent Builds Into a Clothes Survey
fields.features_subheading: Emergent sets up the survey and the app behind it, with branching by garment and an alert on the counts you pick.
fields.feature_1:
Questions written for your clothes

Describe the garments, the people who wear them, and the call the answers feed. Emergent writes the fit and color questions, and a follow-up prompt rewrites any one of them.
fields.feature_2:
Skip logic by garment and size

The survey branches on earlier answers. A buyer who kept the jean answers about waist and length, and one who sent it back is asked why, with their size already filled in.
fields.feature_3:
One question per screen on a phone

Shoppers and parents answer one question per screen on a phone. A fit rating is one tap on a 5-point scale, and a color vote shows every swatch as its own large button.
fields.feature_4:
Responses tagged by style and size

Every response is a row in a database you own, tagged with the style, the size ordered, and the order date. Filter the Dace jean in size 32 without merging two spreadsheets.
fields.feature_5:
An alert when a count crosses your line

Set a line, for example a style where over half its replies say it runs small. The merchandiser gets a Slack or email alert once it is crossed, naming the style and the count.
fields.feature_6:
On your domain, with code export

Put the survey on your own domain, included in Emergent and billed in credits. No cap applies to responses, and paid plans export the full code to your GitHub repository.

fields.tab_content_1:
The Dace page now tells buyers to size up

Sawtell Denim wants to know why buyers send back its Dace straight jean. Ten days after delivery, a fit survey goes to the 260 buyers of the Dace. Each rates the waist, hip, and length from too small to too big. Of the 118 who answer, 64 say the waist runs small. The product page now tells buyers to size up.
fields.tab_content_2:
Of 205 votes, rust takes 88 and the fall run

Before the fall run, Purlwood Knits has to pick the color for its wool crew sweater. A vote goes to 300 newsletter subscribers, with each color shown as a photo swatch. Of the 205 who vote, 88 pick rust and 51 pick oat. Rust gets the larger order from the mill, and oat gets a short run.
fields.tab_content_3:
Polos over blazers, by 201 votes to 111

Hartsdell Middle School has a uniform decision and a board vote in March. The parent council sends a survey to 450 families, and the school roster keeps it to a single answer per family. Of 312 families, 201 choose a polo with any dark pants and 111 a blazer set. The council takes the polo option to the board.
fields.tab_content_4:
96 classmates who buy secondhand, and why

For a term paper on secondhand clothes, a sociology student surveys 150 classmates. The survey asks whether they bought clothes secondhand in the past 6 months, and why. All 150 answer, and 96 say yes. Price comes first for 58 of the 96. The bar chart in the paper is drawn from the response table.

fields.howto_title: How to Write Clothes Survey Questions
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to write clothes survey questions that people finish and that end in a clear call on fit or color.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Ask people who hold the garment
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Rate one fit area per question
fields.howto_step_1_des: Name the call the answers will make before you write a question, such as which color to order or which uniform to propose. Put that decision in your prompt, and Emergent drafts the questions that feed it. Leave out anything that does not.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Fit questions only work from someone wearing the clothes. Send a fit survey a week or two after delivery, never at checkout. For a uniform or a color vote, ask the people who will buy or wear it, and nobody else.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Ask about the waist and the length in separate questions. Pew Research Center's survey guide says it is also important to ask only one question at a time. A rating that covers both areas gives the pattern maker nothing to fix.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Show 4 color swatches, not 12. Pew Research Center's guide says the number of answer choices should be kept to a relatively small number. If the top 2 colors land within a few votes, run a second vote between them.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Use plain words on the fit scale
fields.howto_step_5_des: Label each point on the fit scale in words a shopper uses: runs small, fits, runs big. Pew Research Center found that even small wording differences can substantially affect the answers people provide. Keep the labels identical on every survey you send.
fields.howto_step_6_des: When you cannot guess the reasons people give, send an open question to 20 people first. Pew notes that researchers will sometimes conduct a pilot study using open-ended questions to discover which answers are most common. Turn the common answers into choices.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Act on the count you set
fields.howto_step_7_des: Before launch, write down the count that changes something, such as more than half the replies on a style saying the waist runs small. When the results cross it, update the product page or the order and record the change beside the results.

faq_plan.a: Clothes survey questions ask people about the clothes they buy, wear, or plan to buy: how a garment fits, which color they prefer, why they sent something back, or which uniform they want. Brands use them for fit and color calls, and schools use them to set uniform policy.

faq_plan.q: How do I create clothes survey questions?
faq_plan.a: Start with the decision the answers will feed, then write one question per fit area or option. With Emergent's AI survey builder, you describe the survey in a prompt, and Emergent writes each question and sets up the database behind it. A follow-up prompt changes any question before you send it.

faq_plan.q: What are good clothes survey questions about shopping habits?
faq_plan.a: Good questions each ask about a single habit or choice: how often someone buys clothes, where they shop, what they spend on a typical piece, and what makes them keep or return it. Pair each closed question with an optional open one that asks why.

faq_plan.q: What clothes survey questions work for fit feedback?
faq_plan.a: A fit survey asks which size the person ordered and the size they usually wear, then rates each fit area on its own scale, such as waist, hip, and length for pants. End by asking whether they kept the item. The app Emergent builds stores every answer in a database you own.

faq_plan.q: How many clothes survey questions should one survey have?
faq_plan.a: Aim for 10 questions or fewer, so a shopper can finish in one sitting. A color vote needs a single question, while a research survey for a class paper can run longer when each question feeds the analysis. Emergent puts no cap on how many people respond.

faq_plan.q: Should clothes survey questions ask for body measurements?
faq_plan.a: Ask for measurements only when the decision needs them, such as grading a new size range. For fit feedback, the size ordered, the usual size, and a rating per fit area are enough. Make any measurement question optional, and say how the numbers will be used.

faq_plan.q: How do I write clothes survey questions for a school uniform vote?
faq_plan.a: Ask a single question that names each uniform option, with a photo and its price. Tie each family's link to the school roster. The app then accepts one answer per family and lists who has not replied. Close the vote before the board meets. Emergent builds the roster check and the tally from a prompt.

faq_plan.q: Should clothes survey questions use a rating scale or multiple choice?
faq_plan.a: Use a rating scale for how something fits or feels, and multiple choice for a pick such as a color or a reason. Label every point of the scale in words, like too tight, right, and too loose, instead of numbers alone.

faq_plan.q: What clothes survey questions work for a color vote?
faq_plan.a: Ask one question: which color would you buy? List only the colors you can produce in time, and show each as a photo of the real fabric, not a flat chip of color. Let each person vote once, and hide the running count until the vote closes.

faq_plan.q: Can clothes survey questions stay anonymous in a class research project?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Leave out name and email fields, and ask only what the paper needs, such as age range and shopping habits. Tell respondents in the opening line that their answers are anonymous, and check your school's rules for research that involves people.

plan.angle: The top 10 for clothes survey questions is lists and leftovers: Startquestion idea pages with four or five fashion questions, Pinterest pins of Instagram polls, Scribd questionnaires from student projects, a Reddit request for a uni fashion survey, and ProProfs clothing quizzes. None shows a clothes survey answering a real decision. This page covers the four jobs people mean (fit feedback after an online order, a color vote before a production run, a school uniform consultation, and a student research project on secondhand clothes), shows what each one decided, and puts question-writing advice in the how-to and FAQ.
